key_insight: A spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model can make breast ultrasound diagnoses more trustworthy by tying concept predictions to lesion-specific regions instead of irrelevant image areas.
clinical_relevance: This approach aims to improve both diagnostic performance and explainability in breast ultrasound, supporting more anatomically plausible AI assistance for clinicians.
method: Use coarse lesion masks to define two weakly supervised zones: an in-lesion region and a posterior acoustic band.
Train concept maps with a grouped spatial grounding objective to encourage concept evidence in the right anatomy.
Keep the final diagnosis stage interpretable with a linear bottleneck classifier.
evidence_signal: In five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the model improved diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while increasing spatial alignment; a Train-corrupt/Test-clean stress test assessed how annotation quality affects trustworthiness.
watch_item: The method depends on the quality of coarse lesion delineations, so performance and spatial faithfulness may degrade when supervision is noisy or inconsistently annotated.
paper_title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
